from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

            "Higher dimensions define points as hyper-bubbles.",
            "Constraint: sum of squares equals radius squared."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The Concept of Dimension", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        point = Dot(color=WHITE)

        self.play(Create(point), Write(label_0d))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        line = Line(start=LEFT, end=RIGHT, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(line, 'D3')
        label_1d = Text("1D", font_size=24, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(label_1d, 'D4')
        self.play(Transform(point, line), ReplacementTransform(label_0d, label_1d))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        square = Square(color="#0000FF")
        self.place_at_grid(square, 'E3')
        label_2d = Text("2D", font_size=24, color="#0000FF")
        self.place_at_grid(label_2d, 'E4')
        self.play(Transform(point, square), ReplacementTransform(label_1d, label_2d))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#0000FF")
        
        # Remaining lines need color changes
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["High-dimensional volume behaves in counter-intuitive ways.", "N-ball volumes concentrate near the outer shell.", "The hyper-orange's mass exists mostly in the peel."]
        self.setup_layout("The Geometry of High-Dimensional Volume", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Create a unit hypercube in high-D space, color #FF00FF.
        hypercube = Square(color="#FF00FF", fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(hypercube, 'C3', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(hypercube))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show volume calculation formula: V = s^n, color #FFFF00.
        formula = MathTex(r"V = s^n", color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Animate hypercube stretching, illustrating volume changes, color #00FFFF.
        stretch_factor = ValueTracker(1.0)
        hypercube.add_updater(lambda mob: mob.set_width(1.5 * stretch_factor.get_value()))
        
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(stretch_factor.animate.set_value(2.0), run_time=2)
        self.play(stretch_factor.animate.set_value(1.0), run_time=2)
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The 'Curse' and 'Blessing' of Dimensionality", [
            "N-balls and hypercubes exhibit different behaviors.",
            "In high dimensions, spheres lose space in corners.",
            "The center becomes a void for high-dimensional objects."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show data sparsity: A cube and a sphere
        cube = Cube(side_length=1.5, fill_opacity=0.3, color="#FFA500")
        sphere = Sphere(radius=0.7, fill_opacity=0.6, color="#FFA500")
        group1 = VGroup(cube, sphere)
        self.place_at_grid(group1, 'B2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(cube), GrowFromCenter(sphere))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFA500")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight distance concentration: Heatmap/dots in corners
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(point=self.grid['C4'] + np.array([x, y, 0]) * 0.3, color="#FF4500") 
                        for x in [-1, 1] for y in [-1, 1]])
        self.play(FadeIn(dots))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF4500")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Balance scale
        scale = VGroup(Line(LEFT, RIGHT), Line(ORIGIN, UP*0.5)).set_color("#7FFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(scale, 'E4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(scale))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#7FFF00")
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: Summary and Visualization", [
            "3D intuition often fails in high dimensions.",
            "Rely on algebraic constraints, not just visualization.",
            "Higher-dimensional projections continue to spark curiosity."
        ])
        
        # Create visual assets
        shapes = VGroup(
            Dot(point=ORIGIN, color=BLUE),
            Circle(radius=0.5, color=GREEN),
            Sphere(radius=0.5, color=YELLOW)
        ).arrange(RIGHT)
        self.place_in_area(shapes, 'B1', 'C6', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Create(shapes))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF69B4"))
        self.play(shapes.animate.scale(0.1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        final_card = Text("Dimensionality", font_size=48, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(final_card, 'D3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(final_card))
        self.wait(2)

outline.target_audience: University students with a basic understanding of calculus and linear algebra

sections.title: Introduction: The Concept of Dimension
sections.content: Define n-dimensional space (Rn). Briefly review the 2D circle and 3D sphere as precursors to n-spheres. Establish the distance formula (Euclidean norm) as the foundational constraint for points on a surface.
sections.example: Visualize a 'Flatland' character moving from a 2D circle to a 3D bubble, then imagining a higher-dimensional 'hyper-bubble' defined by x₁² + x₂² + ... + xₙ² = r².

sections.title: The Geometry of High-Dimensional Volume
sections.content: Discuss the counter-intuitive behavior of volume as dimensions increase. Introduce the formula for the volume of an n-ball. Explain why, as n approaches infinity, the volume concentrated near the shell changes drastically.
sections.example: Use an animation showing an orange: in 3D, most of the mass is inside. In 100D, almost all the volume of the hyper-orange is concentrated in the thin 'peel' near the surface.

sections.title: The 'Curse' and 'Blessing' of Dimensionality
sections.content: Contrast the behavior of the n-ball with the n-cube (hypercube). Explain that a sphere inscribed in a cube becomes increasingly 'lost' in the corners of the cube as dimensions rise.
sections.example: A squirrel attempting to hide an acorn in the center of a hyper-room: in high dimensions, the corners of the room grow so far away that the 'center' becomes a void.

sections.title: Application: Data Science and Machine Learning
sections.content: Connect high-dimensional spheres to modern technology. Explain how high-dimensional geometry is used to define similarity (Cosine similarity) and clustering in AI models.
sections.example: A recommendation algorithm treats a user's preferences as a point in 1,000-dimensional space; 'neighbors' on a hyper-sphere represent users with similar tastes.

sections.title: Conclusion: Summary and Visualization
sections.content: Recap the main takeaway: intuition from 3D space fails in high dimensions. Encourage students to rely on algebraic constraints rather than physical visualization.
sections.example: Final slide: A 3D projection of a 4D rotating sphere (tesseract-related geometry) to spark curiosity about non-Euclidean projections.
